subject: Segmentation-based private offer: tiered consumption bundles & reseller margin routing
messages:
From: Claire Novak <claire@datasilo.io>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private offer for segmented customers — pricing options & reseller flow

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're close to defining our Q3 pricing play for two customer segments: Starter (light usage) and Enterprise (burst + reserved). We want to sell through AWS Marketplace, but we also plan to let a handful of resellers (US-only) handle customer onboarding.

Questions before we build the procurement spec:
- Can Redwood support a single private offer with two consumption tiers (Starter / Enterprise) that map to different per-token rates?
- How do we surface reseller margins in the private offer invoice path? We need the reseller payout to be 12% net-of-tax on consumed spend, but we want the customer-facing list price to reflect the bundle.
- Are there limits on SKU mapping for reserved capacity vs metered usage in the same private offer?

Attached is a short sketch of the expected volume mix and target ASPs. Can you share an example structure and any evidence you need for Marketplace approval?

Goal: lock a private offer draft and reseller routing map this week so procurement can start.

Cheers,
Claire Novak
Head of Cloud Procurement
DataSilo Inc
Attachments: volume_sketch.pdf (ref)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Claire Novak <claire@datasilo.io>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-31T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer for segmented customers — pricing options & reseller flow

Hi Claire — great to hear from you and glad the demo was useful. Short answers up front: yes, and yes with some guardrails.

Overview of recommended approach (high level):
1) Single private offer with two SKUs: Starter (metered low-rate) and Enterprise (metered higher-rate + reserved capacity SKU for committed baseline). The private offer can present them as a bundled product in the UI.
2) Reseller routing: AWS supports distributor/reseller pass-through via invoice routing. For your requested 12% net-of-tax reseller payout we normally recommend mapping a separate accounting SKU for the reseller fee so MarketplaceGross -> ResellerFee deduction is automated in downstream settlements.
3) SKU limits: You can mix reserved + metered items; the caveat is billing reconciliation and S3-style billing lines can increase invoice line counts. We can provide a template mapping to avoid issues.

I've attached a working pricing_matrix_v3.xlsx and a draft private offer (privoffer-draft.pdf) that shows how we'd present the two tiers. Helpful evidence for Marketplace approval: your reseller feed agreement (short PDF), a list of reseller tax IDs, and the proposed invoice routing email.

Proposed next steps:
- If comfortable, sign off on the three attachments so we can prepare the Marketplace submission.
- I'll loop in Irene and Ben from Deal Ops to confirm reseller routing, tax offsets, and whether we need an intermediary distributor SKU to handle the 12% payout cleanly.

Would you be available for a 30-min call Thursday morning to finalize?

Best,
Jonas Weber
Head of Marketplace Sales
Redwood Inference
Attachments: pricing_matrix_v3.xlsx, privoffer-draft.pdf

Subject: Fwd: Private offer for segmented customers — pricing options & reseller flow

Irene / Ben — forwarding DataSilo's ask (see original below). Key constraints: customer wants two consumption tiers in a single private offer and a 12% reseller payout net-of-tax.

Questions for Deal Ops / Finance:
- Ben, can we support a reseller-fee SKU that is automatically deducted in Marketplace settlements? If not, what workaround (intermediary distributor SKU, negative line item, platform-managed rebate) would keep the customer's invoice clean but ensure 12% to the reseller?
- Irene, any compliance evidence or Marketplace ops paperwork we should pre-populate (tax IDs, reseller agreement template)? Also flag any EU data residency concerns (customer is US HQ but some EU customers).

Claire is keen to sign by Friday so procurement can route. Attaching our working matrix and a sketch of the routing map.

Thanks — Jonas

--- Original message from Claire Novak <claire@datasilo.io> on 2027-05-30 09:12 ---

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-01T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private offer for segmented customers — pricing options & reseller flow

Thanks for the ping. Quick notes:
- Marketplace: AWS will accept mixed metered + reserved items in one private offer; the only real operational friction is invoice line count and reconciliation windows. We should keep the reserved commitment as a separate line (committed node-hour SKU).
- Reseller payout: We prefer to avoid negative line items in the customer's invoice. Best practice is an explicit ResellerFee SKU that is invoiced as part of the Marketplace settlement but mapped to an internal cost centre for payout. That lets the customer's list price be unchanged and keeps accounting traceable.
- Tax: 12% "net-of-tax" means we need reseller tax IDs and the reseller's billing address country for withholding determination. We'll request reseller W-9 / W-8 forms as appropriate.
- Ops: ask the customer for a list of reseller partner emails (for invoice routing) and a named contact at AWS Marketplace if they have a dedicated rep.

I'll draft the reseller-fee SKU nomenclature and a short ops playbook (2 pages) for the client. Ben, can you estimate the AR / cashflow latency if we route via AWS vs via a distributor? That will affect their onboarding economics.

Irene Choi
Director, Deal Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Claire Novak <claire@datasilo.io>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, AWS Marketplace Ops <aws-marketplace@amazon.com>
Date: 2027-06-02T15:48:00-07:00
Subject: Final: Private offer structure & required evidence (starter / enterprise + reseller routing)

Hi Claire — thanks for the quick responses and for lining up the resellers. Summary and attachments below are the minimal package we need to prepare your Marketplace submission and legal:

What we'll submit to Marketplace (summary):
- Private offer with three SKUs: Starter (metered), Enterprise (metered), Committed Baseline (reserved). Visualized as a single bundle in the purchase flow.
- ResellerFee SKU (12% net-of-tax) mapped to a separate billing line and routed to your listed reseller emails for downstream payout. This preserves your customer-facing list prices.
- Evidence: reseller partner list (with tax forms), reseller agreement (signed or redlined), and the invoice routing email addresses.

Attachments included: pricing_matrix_v3.xlsx (finalized rates by tier and expected monthly spend ranges), privoffer-draft.pdf (UI + SKU mapping), reseller-routing-map.csv (partner emails + tax status).

Operational notes:
- If DataSilo wants the reseller to receive funds faster, consider an intermediary distributor who handles immediate payout and invoices Redwood monthly (this reduces reseller latency but adds ~7-14 day float and a 1-2% platform fee).
- We'll need a single point of contact from DataSilo for procurement sign-off and the W-9/W-8 documents.

Next steps:
1) Claire — please confirm you approve the attached pricing matrix and share reseller tax docs.
2) If approved, we'll prepare the Marketplace submission and share the DocuSign link for the reseller addendum.
3) I'll schedule a 30-min ops walkthrough with Irene + Ben to walk your procurement team through the settlement cadence.

Available times for the walkthrough: Thu 10:00-11:00am PT or Fri 9:00-10:30am PT — which works?

Best,
Jonas Weber
Head of Marketplace Sales
Redwood Inference
